observation_summary: The getLInfNorm() method in both ArrayRealVector and OpenMapRealVector produced incorrect results because the implementation of the L-infinity norm calculation was logically flawed.
reasoning_summary: The bug was caused by an incorrect implementation of the L-infinity norm algorithm. In ArrayRealVector, the code used an incorrect accumulation operator ('+=') instead of an assignment ('='), and in OpenMapRealVector, the logic was fundamentally incorrect (summing values instead of finding the maximum). These are procedural errors in the computation logic, which fits the definition of Algorithm/Method.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'the L_infinity norm of a finite dimensional vector is just the max of the absolute value of its entries.'
The fix diff for ArrayRealVector shows: 'max += Math.max(max, Math.abs(a));' changed to 'max = Math.max(max, Math.abs(a));'
The fix diff for OpenMapRealVector shows the entire incorrect method was removed, as it was not correctly implementing the L-infinity norm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing an assignment operator, the root cause is the incorrect algorithmic logic used to compute the norm, not just an incorrectly initialized variable.
